title: Components with typed props
summary: Build a typed product card that renders props without hiding the data contract.

scenario.briefing: A campus storefront renders product data. Build the card as a typed function component and keep rendering pure.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Declare a ProductProps type with name and price.
Destructure name and price in the parameter list.
Return an article with a heading and a paragraph.

misconceptions.feedback: Props belong to the parent. Emit an event or call a callback instead of writing to them.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Assigning to props leaves the parent's state unchanged and React warns about the read-only value.

misconceptions.description: Rendering a raw float as the price.
misconceptions.feedback: Prices need a fixed display format. Format at the render boundary with toFixed(2).
misconceptions.testDescription: The component renders the name and a two-decimal price.

misconceptions.description: Believing a child may write to a prop to update the parent.
misconceptions.feedback: Props are read-only inputs. A child requests a change through an event or callback; it never assigns to the prop.

sections.title: Props are a contract
sections.body: A component receives data through props. The prop type documents what the component needs and lets the compiler catch missing or misspelled fields.

sections.title: Rendering is a pure step
sections.body: Given the same props, the component should produce the same markup. Side effects belong in event handlers or controlled effects, not in the render path.

sections.title: Small components compose
sections.body: A card that only renders its props can be reused in a list, a detail view, or a checkout summary without changes.

vocabulary.definition: A reusable function that returns markup for a piece of the interface.
A value passed from a parent component to a child.
A render that produces the same markup for the same props.

steps.title: Render a typed product card
steps.prompt: Edit ProductCard.tsx. Type the props, destructure them in the parameter list, and render the name and a price with two decimals.

tests.description: The component keeps a typed props contract and destructures it.
includes: export function ProductCard({ name, price }: ProductProps)

tests.description: The component renders the name and a two-decimal price.

hints: Start from the existing ProductProps type and keep the component exported.
Destructure name and price in the parameter list so the signature matches the contract.
Return a single article element containing a heading and a paragraph.
Render {name} in the heading and {price.toFixed(2)} in the paragraph.

steps.title: Props and rendering

statements.label: Props are read-only inputs supplied by the parent.
A child component should mutate a prop object to update the parent.
A pure render produces the same output for the same props.
A prop type documents the data a component requires.
Every value in a component must be stored in global state.

steps.explanation: Props carry data into a component and remain owned by the parent. A typed signature makes the contract explicit, and a pure render keeps the output predictable.
hints: Read each statement against the props contract, not against a component you might build later.
Eliminate statements that let a child write to props.
Keep statements about pure renders and explicit data contracts.
Select exactly the statements that remain true after those checks.
